elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: § 8.1(ii) still imposes "a minimum monthly fee (\"Monthly Base Fee\")" and amended § 10.3(A) still requires Customer to "obtain from M&I all of those Services which are included in the Monthly Base Fee" during the then-current twelve-month period. A commitment therefore survives, narrowed rather than eliminated.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: The retained payment mechanic requires all minimum monthly fees to be paid "in advance on the first day of the calendar month" by ACH debit regardless of actual consumption, so payment is not limited to usage or ordered Services.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: § 10.3(A) as rendered: "Customer agrees that, during the then-current twelve (12) month period of the Term only, Customer shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services which are included in the Monthly Base Fee" — replaces the prior "during the Term" (eight years) lock.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Customer may reduce the Services included in the Monthly Base Fee, and the corresponding Monthly Base Fee commitment, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to M&I." The right is unconditional and runs in Customer's favour with the required 30-day notice period.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Any resulting shortfall shall be handled solely through a true-up of the Monthly Base Fee to the Services actually ordered and used, and not as a penalty." No shortfall penalty or liquidated formula is retained for the commitment itself.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the term-limitation, the 30 days' notice reduction right, and the true-up-not-penalty treatment are all present in operative language rather than merely promised in the comment.

Preferred level is not reached and the drafter correctly did not claim it: the Monthly Base Fee minimum and its advance ACH payment mechanic in §§ 8.1(ii)/8.13 survive, so Customer still pays a minimum independent of usage. This is an acceptable fallback landing under the playbook (deviation cured to fallback).

Minimality holds: the only textual change to existing wording is "during the Term" → "during the then-current twelve (12) month period of the Term only" in § 10.3(A), plus one concise two-sentence insertion carrying the reduction right and the true-up. The Estimated Remaining Value definition and § 8.1/8.13 payment mechanics are reproduced unchanged (context only), and no survival tails, expense allocation, extra remedies, or out-of-checklist requirements were added.

Intent preserved: the volume-based additional-charge mechanic, the advance-payment/ACH mechanics, the 30-day invoice terms and the collection-fee provision all survive without contradiction; the retained Estimated Remaining Value formula operates only on termination under § 11.1 and is a separate termination-fee issue, so it does not contradict the new no-penalty shortfall treatment for the commitment.

Drafting nit to tighten (not a failure): "then-current twelve (12) month period of the Term" is not an expressly defined division of the eight-year Term. Consider anchoring it to "the then-current twelve (12) month period commencing on the Effective Date or an anniversary thereof" so the reduction right cannot be argued to run against an undefined period.
